title: Sort sensor readings by value
prompt: A sensor report should list values from largest to smallest. Return a sorted copy; keep the caller’s vector unchanged. Empty input stays empty.
driver: int main(){ std::vector<int> v; int n; while(std::cin>>n)v.push_back(n); for(int x:descending(v))std::cout<<x<<" "; std::cout<<"\n"; }

tests.label: Unsorted readings
tests.hint: The default sort order is increasing.

tests.label: Empty
tests.hint: An empty range needs no special index.

tests.label: Negative readings
tests.hint: Do not assume sensor values are positive.

tests.label: Caller remains unchanged
tests.hint: Sort a copy, not the borrowed vector.

hints: std::sort takes two iterators that mark the start and end.
A greater-than comparison asks sort to put larger values first.
explanation: A const reference borrows readings without copying or changing them. The local copy owns the sorted values. This follows the chapter’s value-type sensor example.
chapterTitle: Understanding C++ and How Programs Become Executables
